record.original_question: For finite-energy blow-up families of solutions to the Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a general bounded domain Omega, what asymptotic behavior can occur at a fixed positive parameter lambda, possibly under additional assumptions such as convexity or even strict star-shapedness of Omega?

evidence.quote: Besides, as far as we know the complete scenario of sign-changing solutions has been obtained only in the ODE setting by Esposito, Ghoussoub, Pistoia and Vaira in [27] in dimensions N >= 7 and by Amadori, Gladiali, Grossi, Pistoia and Vaira [2] in lower dimensions 3 <= N <= 6, which completes the previous works of Atkinson, Brezis and Peletier [3] and Iacopetti and Pacella [32, 33].

Open question 7: In a general bounded domain Omega, if necessary, it could be convex or even strictly star-sharped, what is the asymptotic behavior of blow-up solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) with finite energy at a fixed parameter lambda > 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N \geq 3$, let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth domain (which may be assumed convex, or even strictly star-shaped, if needed), and let $2^* = \frac{2N}{N-2}$ denote the critical Sobolev exponent. Consider the Brezis–Nirenberg problem
$$
\begin{cases}
-\Delta u = \lambda u + |u|^{2^*-2} u & \text{in } \Omega,\\
u = 0 & \text{on } \partial \Omega,
\end{cases}
$$
with parameter $\lambda > 0$ fixed. Suppose $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \subset H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a family of (possibly sign-changing) weak solutions of this problem at a fixed $\lambda > 0$ that blows up, i.e. $\|u_n\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \to \infty$, while having uniformly bounded energy
$$
E(u_n) = \frac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u_n|^2 \, dx - \frac{\lambda}{2}\int_\Omega u_n^2 \, dx - \frac{1}{2^*}\int_\Omega |u_n|^{2^*}\, dx \leq C < \infty.
$$
Determine the complete asymptotic behavior of such finite-energy blow-up sequences: classify the possible numbers, locations, signs, and profiles of the bubbles, the rates at which their concentration parameters degenerate, and the relationships these quantities satisfy with $\lambda$ and the geometry of $\Omega$ (in particular, the Robin function of $\Omega$).
artifact.status_search_result: The asymptotic analysis of finite-energy blow-up solutions to the Brezis–Nirenberg problem in general bounded domains at fixed $\lambda > 0$ is only fully understood in radial/ODE settings (works by Atkinson–Brezis–Peletier, Iacopetti–Pacella, Esposito–Ghoussoub–Pistoia–Vaira for $N \geq 7$, and Amadori–Gladiali–Grossi–Pistoia–Vaira for $3 \leq N \leq 6$). For general (e.g. convex or strictly star-shaped) domains the complete asymptotic scenario remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Sign changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
status_evidence.snippet: Amadori, Gladiali, Grossi, Pistoia, Vaira complete the asymptotic analysis of radial sign-changing solutions in dimensions 3≤N≤6 in the ball.
status_evidence.claim: The complete blow-up scenario is currently known only in the radial (ODE) setting.

status_evidence.title: Esposito, Ghoussoub, Pistoia, Vaira - blow-up of sign-changing solutions
status_evidence.snippet: Provides classification of blow-up of radial sign-changing solutions for N≥7 in the ball.
status_evidence.claim: In high dimensions N≥7, the radial case is settled, supporting that the general-domain question is still open.
